summary: France beat Italy at the Rugby World Cup in Lyon, scoring eight tries to top Pool A and reach the quarter-finals, with wing Damian Penaud scoring two. Italy coach Kieran Crowley's tenure ended in disappointment, and he criticised the Italian federation's treatment of players. Fabien Galthié said the quarter-final would be like a second World Cup final and expects Antoine Dupont and Julien Marchand back in the knockout stages.
one_line: France thrash Italy with eight tries, led by Damian Penaud's double, to win Pool A and advance to the World Cup quarter-finals.
key_facts: France scored eight tries against Italy and secured top spot in Pool A, reaching the quarter-finals.
Damian Penaud scored the first try in the second minute and added a second, taking him to 35 French try-scorer tries, three behind Serge Blanco.
Penaud has scored in seven straight matches and 14 times this year.
France have beaten Italy 14 times consecutively, a run stretching back to 2014.
France led 31-0 at half-time; Penaud's second try secured the bonus point.
Simone Ferrari's try for Italy was chalked off by the television match official for a high hit on Maxime Lucu.
Ange Capuozzo failed his head injury assessment after being removed in the first half.
Italy's consolation try came from Manuel Zuliani and was converted by fly-half Tommaso Allan.
Yoram Moefana came on for Gaël Fickou and scored twice, including France's seventh try on 63 minutes.
Cyril Baille and Jonathan Danty returned from injury and started against Italy; Antoine Dupont is out with a fractured cheekbone.
Galthié said the quarter-final next Sunday would be 'a second final' after the opening-night match against New Zealand, and expects Dupont and Julien Marchand to play in the knockout stages.
Kieran Crowley said Italian players need to be treated with respect off the field and doubted he would want to stay involved unless the federation sorts these issues.
